texts.preamble: O.Aboobaker vs State Of Kerala on 21 March, 2016 Author: B.Sudheendra Kumar Bench: B.Sudheendra Kumar In The High Court Of Kerala At Ernakulam Present: The Honourable Mr. Justice B.Sudheendra Kumar Monday, The 21St Day Of March 2016/1St Chaithra, 1938 Crl.Rev.Pet.No. 3122 of 2009 --------------------------------- Crl.A 130/2007 of Addl.Sessions Court (Adhoc), Mavelikkara St 2/2003 of J.M.F.C.-Ii, Haripad Revision Petitioner/Appellant/Accused: ---------------------------------------------------------------- O.Aboobaker, Aged 65 Years S/O. Ummer Kutty, Maharani Manzil, Poonkudiyil Veettuveni, Haripad. By Adv. Sri.N.A.Muraleedharan Respondents/Respondents/Complainants: ------------------------------------------------------------------ 1. State Of Kerala Public Prosecutor, High Court Of Kerala, Ernakulam. 2. P.Unnikrishnan, Food Inspector, Haripad Circle, Haripad. R1 & R2 By Public Prosecutor, Shri.R.Githesh This Criminal Revision Petition Having Been Finally Heard On 21-03-2016, The Court On The Same Day Passed The Following: B.Sudheendra Kumar, J. - - - - - - - - - - - - - - -- - - -- - - - - - - - - - -- - - - - - - - - Crl.R.P. texts.facts: The prosecution allegation can be briefly stated thus:- On 5.9.2002, PW1, the Food Inspector, purchased one k.g. of banana chips from the revision petitioner. After sampling as per rules, one of the samples was sent for analysis to the Public Analyst. The Public Analyst filed Ext. P13 report stating that the sample contained synthetic food colour Tartrazine and was therefore, adulterated under the Prevention of Food Adulteration Rules, 1955. Thereafter, on the request of the accused, second sample was sent to the Central Food Laboratory for analysis. Ext.P22 certificate of the Central Food Laboratory would also show that the sample contravened Rule 29 of the Food Adulteration Rules, 1955 and therefore, it was adulterated. 4. Before the trial Court, PW1 to PW5 were examined and Exts. P1 to P22 were marked for the prosecution. No evidence was adduced on the side of the revision petitioner.
texts.arguments: 5. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner has submitted that since no laboratory for the analysis of the food item was defined and no validated method of analysis was prescribed as per the mandate of Section 23 (1-A)(ee) and (hh) of the PFA Act, Ext. P22 cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased by the Food Inspector was adulterated. The learned counsel for the revision petitioner relied on the decision of the Apex Court in Pepsico India Holdings (P) Ltd. v. Food Inspector [(2011) 1 SCC 176] to buttress his argument. 6. In this case, admittedly, the laboratory for the analysis of food item was not defined and no validated method of analysis of the food item was prescribed as mandated under Section 23 (1-A) (ee) and (hh) of the P.F.A. Act. Therefore, Ext. P22 certificate of analysis cannot be acted upon to hold that the food item purchased in this case was adulterated in view of the decision of the Apex court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra). It was held by the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) that since the Laboratories were not notified and the tests conducted by such laboratories were not admissible in evidence, no prosecution could be based on such report and the accused was entitled to get acquittal. In the decision of this Court in Gopalakrishnan v. Food Inspector [2013 (3) KLT 455], the court relied on the decision of the Supreme Court in Pepsico India Holdings (supra) and found that the Public Analyst's report was not admissible in evidence and O.Aboobaker vs State Of Kerala on 21 March, 2016 Indian Kanoon - http://indiankanoon.org/doc/167769293/ 2
